title: Design System: Η εβδομάδα μου · ΤΗΜΜΥ

display.purpose: Two-line hero headline only, at poster size in weight 800; line-mask reveal, each line standing up toward the reader.

stat.purpose: Week totals as odometer digits, weight 800.

print-title.purpose: Print only: schedule heading, followed by the season and the data's date at 13px in ink-3.

print-event.purpose: Print only: course names in blocks.

print-meta.purpose: Print only: event times, rooms, day meta.

title.purpose: Panel headings: course rail, weekly schedule.

lede.purpose: Hero sub-sentence (the week's facts once courses are chosen), max 40ch.

body.purpose: Default text, tabular figures; paragraphs at 1.6 line height.

control.purpose: Buttons, selects, menu items, season switch.

meta.purpose: Course meta, sync time, footer, tooltips.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Hovered event blocks (at rest they are flat, with no shadow), the hero tooltip, a block in flight.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, menus, rail drawer, rail button, update toast, and the shadow a dealt block presses down from.

shadows.name: highlight
shadows.purpose: Top-edge highlight paired with floating surfaces (dialogs, menus, drawer, update toast).

motion.name: ease
motion.value: cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: Default expo-out for transitions, entrances, drawers, dialogs, and every exit (exit() in app.js, the EASE constant).

motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: ~5% overshoot for things that settle into a new value or slot: the season thumb, a block shifting to a new slot (520ms). Falls back to the ease curve.

motion.name: there-and-back
motion.value: cubic-bezier(.77,0,.175,1)
motion.purpose: In-out curve for one-shot pulses that leave rest and return to it: the clash pulse. Never for entrances or exits.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Colour, fill and press transitions on controls; press is scale(.96).

motion.name: odometer
motion.value: .6s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), 30ms per-digit stagger
motion.purpose: Stat digits roll to new values (countTo) with no overshoot, so the clipped column never shows its neighbour.

motion.name: flight
motion.value: 660ms; x cubic-bezier(.55,0,.3,1), y cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.25,1)
motion.purpose: Added course flies on an arc from its rail swatch into each new slot (fly()), swelling toward the viewer mid-flight (scale 1 -> 1.2 -> 1 over the flight) and coming down onto its slot; the ghost starts at a 3px corner (swatch-like) and opens to 10px in flight, then the block is revealed with the press-in (block-deal) at +600ms, the flight's landing. A ghost whose course is deselected or whose season is left mid-flight is removed. The 3px is a motion detail, not a radius token.

motion.name: season-redeal
motion.value: old blocks: block-leave, 8ms apart, capped at 120ms (not on the phone agenda); new blocks: block-deal from 120ms, min(40, 360/n)ms apart by day (about .5s in all); 3D: old slabs shrink away, new slabs come in from the viewer's side of the glass with the squash, 40ms apart (tile-deal)
motion.purpose: Season switch re-deals the week; it replaces the 3D page-turn view transition, now removed. While the 3D week stands in for the blocks it lands in 3D alone. Instant under reduced motion.

motion.name: detail-morph
motion.value: .4s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) view transition (group)
motion.purpose: Course dialog grows out of the clicked block or title (morphOpen()).

motion.name: pop-in
motion.value: scale(.96) translateY(-4px) to rest; data menu .2s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), notices and the update report .25s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: Menus and notices popping in.

motion.name: dialog-exit
motion.value: desktop: opacity 0, translateY(8px) scale(.98), 160ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); phone sheets: translateY(100%), 200ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); backdrop opacity .16s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) (dialog.closing::backdrop)
motion.purpose: closeDialog() via exit(): every close path (buttons, Escape through the cancel event, finished actions) animates out, then closes. Entry is dialog-in .28s var(--ease) from perspective(1100px) translate3d(0,14px,-90px) rotateX(5deg) (desktop: it comes forward out of the page) / phone sheet-up .38s cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1).

motion.name: block-leave
motion.value: 180ms; opacity on the CSS ease keyword cubic-bezier(.25,.1,.25,1) (readable fade; the ease-out would empty it in about two frames), scale(1.04) on var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: A removed block lifts away where it stood (leave()). Desktop grid only; skipped where another block moves into the freed rect and when the week becomes empty. A season switch lifts every old block away this way (season-redeal).

motion.name: clash-pulse
motion.value: outline-offset -2px -> -6px -> -2px, 400ms there-and-back, once; delay = landing (600ms + stagger after a flight, 150ms + stagger after a dealt block)
motion.purpose: Only a block already on the week that has just become conflicting pulses; the newcomer never does. Same season only.

motion.name: toast
motion.value: in: toast-in .28s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) from translate(-50%,-10px) scale(.96); out: same transform with opacity 0, 200ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: Update toast eases in from above and leaves upward the way it came.

motion.name: hero-reveal
motion.value: line-in .9s var(--ease) from translateY(110%) rotateX(64deg) about the baseline (900px perspective on the mask), .1s/.19s stagger; sub and CTA fade-up .6s at .3s/.38s; sheet-in 1.2s at .36s from translateY(9svh)
motion.purpose: First-viewport entrance: the poster's title stands up line by line at the top left, the facts and the action rise at the foot, and the sheet slides up under them.

motion.name: scroll-linked
motion.value: animation-timeline: scroll(root)
motion.purpose: Hero copy recedes over 60svh (scale .9 about its top-left corner, 4svh up, fading out), the header's sheet-coloured ground fades in (no edge line) as the sheet docks, rail button rises as the sheet docks.

motion.name: scroll-morph
motion.value: p follows the scroll on a critically damped spring (k 160, c 25.3), never 1:1, so a fast or back-and-forth scroll plays at the motion's own pace; e = smooth((p - .04) / .84); labels out e .35-.65; board/edges dissolve e .55-.95; slab tops to flat fill e .3-.9; planner chrome in e .82-.97 (--chrome); blocks crossfade p .9-1 (--blocks), held at 0 while a deal or throw runs (a dealt block shows on its own via --dealt); the crossfade share itself is eased (16/s), so it never pops when a deal or throw ends
motion.purpose: Above 860px the fixed 3D stage (z 2, pointer-events none, clip-path path evenodd cutting the toolbar/stats band and docked rail) swings the camera straight down and lands the board on the live rect of the planner day columns, the lens closing from 36 to 24 degrees with e (lerped) while the camera backs off to match (a dolly zoom: the board keeps its size, its perspective drains out; the landing stays exact); slabs flatten (y scale .03) and take the exact flat fill of their blocks (emissive = DOM fill; albedo, clearcoat and env drop). Docked: stage hidden, rendering stops until a 1px .dock-mark just above the docking point (placed by measure(), watched by an IntersectionObserver; hidden in print, removed from the HTML backup) comes into view, a resize, or the drawer closing. Reverses on scroll up. Phones: tilt-away under the sheet. Focus in the week or print forces the 2D week visible.

motion.name: free-view
motion.value: pointerdown catches (aim = current pose); held: yaw/pitch spring to aim (170/19); throw keeps spring velocity soft-limited by m*tanh(v/m) (m 12 yaw, 2.8 pitch; 0 under reduced motion), then drag exp(-dt*3.2) plus constant grip 2.6 rad/s^2 (flick 3 rad/s -> 32deg in .48s, 8 -> 95deg .70s, 16 -> 153deg .82s, 30 -> 177deg .87s); a thrown tilt stays within the same .1 rubber stretch (peak .098), never reaching the elevation clamp; yaw free; pitch [-.4, .86] on a .56 rad base, rubber band past it (STRETCH .1, asymptotic) with spring-back 160/18; camera elevation clamped [.06, pi/2-.04]; zoom eases to aim (120/18); zoom [.8, 1.6] by pinch or Ctrl+wheel; 5px drag threshold; double-click resets
motion.purpose: Hero board free view. Touch: horizontal swipes spin, vertical swipes scroll (.hero touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom). Free view starts only at the top (scroll progress <= 0.002); a drag still held when the page scrolls yields to the homing spring. Orbit springs home once scroll progress > 0 and its offsets scale by (1 - e), so the landing stays exact. A press that travels more than 5px never opens a course.

motion.name: free-view-feel
motion.value: lift .24 while dragging (95/15), one small settle on release (150/13); bank from yaw velocity (clamp .16) and nod from pitch velocity (clamp .12), 110/13; jelly lean rx/rz per slab 170/14 scaled by slab height and distance from centre; squash scale.y from lift velocity (clamp .14); all times calm (1 - e)
motion.purpose: Pseudo-physics weight on the hero board. Reduced motion: drag sets the pose directly, no throw, lift, settle or jelly.

motion.name: drawer-handoff
motion.value: body.rail-open
motion.purpose: Open tablet drawer or phone sheet: 3D stage hidden and not rendered (treated as docked); planner forced fully in (--chrome:1, --blocks:1, empty state opaque) so the fixed layer never draws over the drawer.

motion.name: copy-clearance
motion.value: spring pan; each part of the copy (a title line, the facts, the button) cleared on its own: board quad >= 12px right of that part at its own height (12px above the facts on phones); fades out as e rises
motion.purpose: Keeps title, facts and action in front at any orbit or zoom; the board's corner may stand under the title's long first line, beside the short second one. The home pose needs no pan.

motion.name: slab-height
motion.value: h = .18 + (min(5, n) - 1) * .22 world units
motion.purpose: Slab height encodes weekly meetings n: once is nearly flat, three or more clearly tall.

motion.name: slab-engraving
motion.value: code up to .24 world units (min .09), pad .09; 300px per unit; walls: box blur radius 2px, slope 9; groove shade 1 - .62 x depth; roughness .55, no clearcoat
motion.purpose: The course code engraved, centred, into each real slab top: a normal-mapped groove in the slab colour that catches the scene light as the board turns; narrow tops shrink the code, then drop the ECE prefix; fades with the board labels over e .35-.65.

motion.name: ring-trace
motion.value: .8s ease infinite alternate, outline-offset -3px to -6px
motion.purpose: Conflict trace pulses its red ring inward inside the block.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.value: Lenis lerp .085
motion.purpose: Page smooth scroll; nested scrollers and dialogs stay native.

motion.name: drawer
motion.value: in: transform .5s var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); out: transform .2s var(--ease), visibility hidden at .2s
motion.purpose: Rail side drawer and phone bottom sheet; dialogs rise as sheets on phones. Tabbing out of the drawer closes it. The phone sheet follows a touch dragged down from its handle or heading (no transition while held), closes past 80px or on a downward flick (over 0.5px/ms over the last 16ms or more, released within 100ms of the last move) and otherwise springs back.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
motion.purpose: Removes all CSS animation and transitions, view transitions, Lenis, fly/morph and the scroll morph; exits (dialogs, toast) are instant, and the block lift-away, the deals and the clash pulse are skipped; the 3D week is a still picture (.hero-stage.still) that scrolls away with the hero.

motion.name: tile-fling
motion.value: grip 600 on ω²·(r+1.5)·(1+0.8h), only while held and spun (drag moved, |ω| > 3), held over it for SLIP .25s; gravity 22; one floor bounce; hop back 420-560ms, 40ms stagger by day (18ms when the page scrolls)
motion.purpose: Spinning the hero board too fast by hand flings slabs onto the studio floor, in a layer that turns with the camera; a flick or a released throw never spills (about 800px/s keeps every slab, about 1400px/s held .25s spills the rim, a full-width hard swipe clears the board); once the spin calms they hop back to their slots, Monday to Friday, landing with a squash. Not under reduced motion.

motion.name: tile-throw
motion.value: fires once p < .9, every time the page scrolls up from near the planner (re-arms with the week whole at p >= .95); each leaves along its own line, up and outward from where it sits on screen, to the edge in ~0.3s, closing on the lens by up to seven tenths of its distance (about 3x its size); return from beyond the edge and from 2.2x its landed size, 300ms each, 40ms stagger by day (10ms heading back down); rested = eased progress moving under a fifth of a pixel per frame for 160ms
motion.purpose: Scrolling up from near the planner (docked or not) throws the slabs out of view, up and outward and at the viewer, past the edges of the screen, only once the scroll is below 90% so overshooting the planner's top never throws the week; they come back onto the board when the scroll rests 160ms, the board nears the hero (p < .25) or the page heads back down. Desktop and tablet only; not under reduced motion.

motion.name: tile-deal
motion.value: DEAL 40ms per tile, by day then start time; landing: gravity 22 from the viewer's side of the glass (about 11 units out along the tile's own line of sight to the camera, plus a little from above, so it starts large and close and shrinks onto its slot, tumbling and righting itself), squash .22 (spring 260/16), no overshoot, then a thud that dips and tips the board; intro from 380ms, at most 16 steps; scroll down: lift once p > .05 (intro tiles come along: falling ones lifted where they are, unshown ones keep their moment and arrive from the viewer's side of the glass into the hover), 12ms apart, hover .55 units (spring 240, damping exp(-28·dt)), dealt at e >= .995 (or scroll rest 200ms, scroll up, back at the top), gap min(40, 360/n)ms (about .5s in all), fall 200ms on u·(.35+.65u), then hand-over: tile hides, block --dealt: 1, scale(1.1) -> none from its centre, box-shadow var(--shadow-lg) -> none, 200ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)
motion.purpose: One landing for the 3D tiles: the intro, rebuilds, the hop back after a spin and the return after a throw all land this way. The first committed scroll down from the top (a jiggle never does) lifts the tiles, taking any still in the intro along, and deals them onto the landed planner, each handing over to its own block; the canvas stays on, other blocks stay hidden and the stage does not dock until the deal ends; handed-over tiles come back if the board leaves the landed pose. Desktop and tablet only; not under reduced motion.

motion.name: block-deal
motion.value: opacity 0 -> 1, scale(1.1) -> none from the centre (transform-origin center; blocks keep a top origin for the hover lift), box-shadow var(--shadow-lg) -> none, 240ms var(--ease) cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), fill backwards (stampIn()); DEAL 40ms stagger, at most 12 steps
motion.purpose: One landing for the 2D week's blocks, the echo of the 3D deal: new blocks arrive a touch larger and press down to size, Monday to Friday. A course flying in from the list is revealed this way at the flight's landing. Skipped, like every 2D block animation (lift-away, flight, clash pulse), while the 3D week stands in for the blocks (--blocks below 1, no focus in #calendarWrap): one landing per change. Not under reduced motion.

motion.name: hero-depth
motion.value: lens 36 -> 24 degrees with e, camera backing off to match (dolly zoom), framing: board radius x FIT .7 inside the poster's free box (see hero-framing); load dolly: camera starts 2.1x further back on a spring (34/7) with a small overshoot; thud on every landing: board dips and tips toward the slot (spring 150/11); pointer: camera parallax .26 / .12, key light leans with it (x 4, z 3 units), slabs within reach of the pointer rise up to .2 units (falloff exp(-d²/2.6)), the slab under it .46 on a 240/15 spring; canvas fade .7s, hero skeleton fade .6s, skeleton posed to the 36 degree lens
motion.purpose: Depth along the line of sight in the hero: the lens is wide in the hero and long on the planner, the board arrives from deep in the studio, every landing moves it, and the pointer pulls the slabs and the light. The pointer effects fade with the landing and, like the load and the thud, are off under reduced motion; the still picture draws its shadows on each of its few frames.

motion.name: hero-framing
motion.value: free box, wide: left = end of the title's last line + 2% of the width, top = half-way down its first line, right = 104% of the width, bottom = 95% of the hero (the sheet's edge cuts the board); phones: full width from 4px under the title to 12px above the facts; board radius x FIT .7 inside it, 82% of its width used
motion.purpose: The poster's composition for the 3D week: right of the title's short second line and from half-way down its long first one, out past the right edge and down to the sheet; between the title and the facts on phones. Measured from layout positions, so the copy's entrance and scroll transforms never move it.

motion.name: block-rise
motion.value: animation-timeline: view(), linear; each sign-off block from translateY(104%) to rest, animation-range entry calc(i * 4%) to entry calc(52% + i * 4%) for block i (0 to 12); the field clips at the baseline (overflow: clip); in the two-row phone layout block-up instead: from translateY(30%) and opacity 0
motion.purpose: The page's closing title is built from blocks, one per letter and one for the full stop; as the footer scrolls in they come up from under the baseline one after another, the week dealt one last time. Only where scroll timelines exist (@supports animation-timeline: view()); static otherwise and under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: vertical day agenda, rail as bottom sheet with scrim, dialogs as bottom sheets, 24px sheet radius, 3D tilt-away instead of the scroll morph.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Full-width week, rail as side drawer.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: min-width: docked 340px rail beside the week.

breakpoints.name: lane-time-name
breakpoints.purpose: Narrow lane: start time plus the compact name, soft-hyphenated at Greek syllables (app.js hyphenate). Only lanes this narrow hyphenate; wider lanes wrap whole words (hyphens: none).

breakpoints.name: lane-time-code
breakpoints.value: 80px (container, screen); also lessons of an hour or less below 112px
breakpoints.purpose: Narrower lane: start time plus course code.

breakpoints.name: lane-number
breakpoints.purpose: Four or more parallel lessons: the shared ECE prefix hides, the course number stays.

components.name: Event Block
components.description: A course on the week: a flat field of the full course hue (no lip, rim, inner edge or shadow at rest; the 3D tile is the object, the block is its print), ink or white text by contrast against the fill (the dark-theme mix in dark), meta at full strength; review and conflict rings sit inside the block, the focus ring outside it (an outline, or a shadow ring on a block with a state ring, so the state ring stays visible); review adds a 10px hatched strip at the right edge, clear of the text. Hover lifts 1px to the lifted shadow over 150ms, only on fine hovering pointers; a press scales it to .985.

narrative.overview:
The student's own timetable is a product shot. It sits as glossy 3D slabs on a floating board in a neutral photo studio, lit like an object on a seamless backdrop, and the planner sheet rises over it like a page slid onto the set. Everything around the object stays quiet: studio greys, ink type, one neon accent. The colour lives in the courses themselves. The first screen is composed as a poster: the title sits at the top left at poster size, in the heaviest weight, on the same left edge as the sheet's content; the week stands right of its short second line and from half-way down its long first one, out past the right edge and down to the sheet, whose edge cuts it; and the week's facts and the one action sit at the foot, just above the sheet's edge. The grounds are flat: the studio is one tone and the sheet another, meeting at a seam, with no glow behind the board and no shadow on the sheet's edge. The page closes where it began, on a black field from edge to edge.

Below the fold the studio becomes a calm, editorial work surface. The week is the canvas and is never cropped sideways. Pills for everything you press, soft 20-28px surfaces, 12px event blocks that are flat fields of colour (the 3D tile is the object, the block is its print), giant heavy grotesk numerals for the stats. The signature move is a scroll morph: on desktop and tablet the 3D board swings to a top-down view and lands exactly on the planner's week, and the slabs become its flat blocks. The tiles are objects and the board is their tray: whenever the week changes place or content, the tiles leave the tray and are dealt back Monday to Friday (by day, then start time), 40ms apart and the whole deal held to about half a second, with one landing. In 3D a tile comes in from the viewer's side of the glass, large and close, and shrinks onto its slot, accelerating under gravity, and squashes as it lands; on the 2D week a block arrives a touch larger and presses down to size. The intro, the hop back after a spin, the return after a throw, the scroll down onto the planner, new blocks and the season switch all deal this way. Elsewhere motion is physical and springy: digits roll, the season thumb and blocks moving to a new slot settle with a small overshoot, and a course flies on an arc into its slot, swelling toward the viewer on the way. Exits are shorter than entrances and leave the way things came, on the ease-out: dialogs drop and fade, phone sheets slide back down, a removed block lifts away where it stood, the update toast lifts away. The one exception: a removed block's opacity runs on the CSS `ease` keyword so the fade stays readable, while its scale stays on the ease-out. A block that has just started to clash pulses its red ring once on the there-and-back curve. Every one of these collapses to an instant, static path under reduced motion.

The world is modelled on butter.video, chosen by the user. Rejected and not to return: the cool-grey, electric-blue, pastel-course "premium product app" world set in Commissioner with 16/10 radii.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral studio greys with an off-white (light) or ink (dark) planner sheet; no tinted neutrals.
Ink is the primary action colour; hot pink is a single neon note, never a fill for large surfaces.
Nine vivid course hues, full-strength on event blocks, with ink or white text chosen by contrast.
Geologica everywhere, tabular figures by default, display sizes in the heaviest weight (800) with tight negative tracking.
Pill controls, soft rectangles for surfaces, 12px for event blocks.

Surfaces part by a step of tone, not by lines or resting shadows; only things that really float (dialogs, menus, drawers, tooltips, the rail button, the toast) cast a shadow. Event blocks are flat fields of colour. The calendar grid keeps its lines.

A poster first screen: the title at the top left at poster size on the sheet's left edge, the 3D week right of its short second line and out past the right edge, the facts and the one action at the foot. The studio and the sheet are two flat tones meeting at a seam, with no gradient, glow or shadow between them.
The page closes on a black field in both themes, where the title is rebuilt from blocks in the week's own colours.
The hero's 3D week and the planner's 2D week are one object: scrolling morphs one into the other.

One landing: tiles and blocks are dealt Monday to Friday, 40ms apart, the whole deal held to about half a second; a 3D tile closes from the viewer's side of the glass under gravity and squashes, a 2D block presses from 1.1 to size.

Motion has depth along the line of sight: things arrive from, and leave toward, the viewer's side of the glass (a tile shrinking onto its slot, a throw that comes at the lens, a dialog coming forward out of the page, a headline standing up toward the reader), and nothing just slides in the screen plane; it always resolves to the flat, exact planner.

Three curves: the spring (~5% overshoot) for things that settle into a new value or slot, the ease-out for transitions, presses and exits, the there-and-back in-out for one-shot pulses; everything static under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Neon Rule
rules.body: Hot pink is the only accent and it appears as small marks (a full stop, a day pill, a count, a hover), never as a button fill or a section background. Primary actions are ink.

rules.name: The Colour Is the Course Rule
rules.body: Saturation belongs to the course palette. Chrome stays grey and ink; no course is ever grey, and no course hue is pure green, amber or red, so courses can never be mistaken for a state. A selected rail row borrows its course's hue as an 11% wash, the one place chrome takes a course colour, so the list and the week read as one.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every semantic state carries a second signal: passed is a filled green swatch plus a check icon; review is a dashed amber outline plus a hatched strip; overlap is a solid red outline plus a warning icon.

rules.name: The Numbers Are the Headline Rule
rules.body: Figures are tabular everywhere, and the week's totals are set at display scale, not tucked into small chips.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Geologica carries every role; hierarchy comes from size, weight and tracking, never from a second display face.

rules.name: The No Sideways Week Rule
rules.body: The week never scrolls horizontally. The grid is a 54px hour axis (headed Ώρα) plus five equal day columns, whatever they hold. Parallel lessons split their day into lanes, and narrow lanes step down by container width. At 112px or less a lane shows its start time and the name, set compact with soft hyphens at Greek syllable breaks; wider lanes never hyphenate and wrap whole words. At 80px or less, and for lessons of an hour or less, it shows start time plus course code. At 60px or less it shows the code only. At 50px or less the shared ECE prefix drops and only the course number remains. The full name always stays in the tooltip and dialog. Margin notes move beside the week only when the busiest day still gets 150px per lane. There the checks are a sticky margin note on a `surface-2` panel that mirrors the rail, always open, with their summary as a heading rather than a toggle (out of the tab order).

rules.name: The Print Is Its Own Layout Rule
rules.body: Print is one A4 landscape sheet in the selected theme: chrome hidden, the sheet and blocks exactly as on screen (light or dark), no today marking, the title followed by the season and the data's date, the week scaled to fit and forced fully visible, the print type ramp, all motion, shadows and focus rings off. Nothing on the printed page sizes itself with viewport units, because Chrome's print preview resolves them against the browser window and a window-tall page spills a blank second sheet.

rules.name: The Press, Don't Lift Rule
rules.body: Controls press (scale 0.96 on active) and never rise on hover. Only event blocks lift (1px, over 150ms, to the lifted shadow) on hover, as the pieces of the week itself, and only where a fine pointer can hover ((hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)), so a tap never leaves a block stuck raised.

rules.name: The Rings Inside Rule
rules.body: State and highlight outlines on event blocks sit inside the block (negative offset), never outside it. Keyboard focus is the one ring outside: the 2px ink outline offset 2px, raised above the neighbouring lanes. A block with a state ring keeps it, and its focus ring is a shadow outside the block (a 2px sheet gap, then 2px ink), so a focused clash still shows red.

rules.name: The Hairline in the Dark Rule
rules.body: In dark mode every floating surface (dialog, menu, tooltip, drawer) gets a 1px hairline edge, since shadows cannot read on ink.

dos: **Do** make primary actions ink pills; keep hot pink to small marks (full stop, today, counts, hover).
**Do** give every pressable thing a full pill shape and the 0.96 press.
**Do** let free-view interactions (orbit, zoom) yield to scroll and to the copy: plain wheel scrolls, the board springs home on scroll, and it never covers the headline.
**Do** pick block text colour by contrast (ink or white) for any course hue, including user-chosen ones, measured against the fill the text sits on (the dark-theme mix in dark mode).
**Do** pair every success, warning and danger state with an icon, dashes or an outline.

**Do** use the spring easing (`linear()` with ~5% overshoot, fallback cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)) for things that settle into a new value or slot (digits, the season thumb, a block shifting lanes), the ease-out (cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)) for the 2D press-in and for exits, and the there-and-back curve (cubic-bezier(.77,0,.175,1)) only for one-shot pulses that return to rest; make every animation, view transition, smooth scroll and 3D loop disappear under reduced motion.

**Do** deal tiles and blocks onto the week Monday to Friday (by day, then start time), 40ms apart and the whole deal held to about half a second (bigger weeks close the gap), with one landing per change: in 3D an arrival from the viewer's side of the glass that accelerates under gravity and ends in a squash, never a spring that overshoots into the board; in 2D a press from scale 1.1 to size about the block's centre, with a fade and the floating shadow coming away as the block lies flat (240ms on the ease-out). While the 3D week stands in for the planner's blocks, the change lands in 3D alone.

**Do** make exits shorter than their entrances (160-200ms) and send things out the way they came in, on the ease-out; the one exception is a removed block, whose opacity runs on the CSS `ease` keyword so the fade stays readable while its scale stays on the ease-out. For the opposite direction use mirrored keyframes, never `animation-direction: reverse`, which turns the ease-out into an ease-in.
**Do** keep five equal day columns and step narrow lanes down (time and name, time and code, code, number) rather than widening a busy day.
**Do** keep the week fully visible without horizontal scroll at every width, and keep print as a dedicated A4 landscape layout.
**Do** keep the 3D week and the planner's week the same object: same course colours, the same five equal columns and lanes, one hand-over sequence with never two hour axes on screen.
**Do** use tabular figures and display-scale numerals for the week's totals.

**Do** keep the first screen a poster: the title at poster size at the top left on the page margin (`--gutter`), the facts and the one action at the foot just above the sheet's edge, the week in the space between and beside them, never behind the copy.
**Do** keep grounds and blocks flat: the studio and the sheet are two flat tones meeting at a seam, and an event block is a field of its course colour.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent colour or fill buttons, panels or headers with neon pink.
**Don't** use grey, pure green, amber or red as a course colour.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or uppercase tracked labels; Geologica in sentence case carries every role.
**Don't** use square or small-radius buttons; nothing pressable sits between pill and rectangle.
**Don't** lift controls on hover or use hard offset shadows; controls press, only event blocks lift.
**Don't** draw state or highlight rings outside an event block.
**Don't** tint the neutrals cool or warm; the studio greys are neutral.
**Don't** put a gradient, glow, shadow or top line between the studio and the sheet, or a lip, rim, inner edge or resting shadow on an event block.
